newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end firmer, caution pervades ahead of tankan. [CORRECTED 08:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: JGBs end firmer, caution pervades ahead of tankan. [CORRECTED 08:50 GMT]

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract ended slightly higher on Thursday, supported by buying of long-term cash bonds in the afternoon.
"There was talk that a public fund sold medium-term bonds and replaced them with 190th to 196th JGBs...during the afternoon session," a brokerage house trader said.

The Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd's June five-year bank debentures with a coupon rate of two percent were traded at a yield of 1.94 percent on Thursday, compared with Wednesday's close of 1.98 percent, traders said.
The September ended at 124.06, up slightly from Wednesday's close of 123.99. Turnover was 30,117 contracts.

Bank debentures were sold on Wednesday following a domestic newspaper report saying funds from the Fiscal Investment and Loan Programme had not been used to buy interest-bearing bank debentures since April and that purchases of discount debentures would also be halted within the next year or two.

The yield of the June IBJ five-year debentures rose as high as 2.01 percent on Wednesday. Finance Ministry officials denied that MOF was planning to stop buying debentures after the market closed on Wednesday, triggering buying on dips today.

"I think investors want to buy (debentures). Even yesterday, when dealers were in a hurry to sell debentures, investors just called to ask for the level of the market and refrained from actually selling," a trader for a trust bank's securities unit.
Investors are probably attracted to the debentures' high yields relative to JGBs with similar maturities, the trader said.
The 148th 10-year JGB which has about five years left until maturity was tagged with a buy quote of 1.680 percent on Wednesday. No bids or offers were detected on Thursday.
The suspension of Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd from JGB auctions and JGB underwriting announced by MOF on Wednesday is not expected to have a large impact on JGBs, traders said.

"Combined with the suspension of Nomura Securities, it may mean that there are fewer chances that JGB auctions will become overheated, but overall there probably will not be much of an effect," a trader for a city bank's securities unit said.

Traders said MOF is likely to hold an auction for 10-year JGBs next Tuesday. Judging from current market conditions, they said the coupon rate is likely to be set at 2.6 percent, down (corrects from up) from 2.7 percent for the most recent 196th 10-year JGB.

If the coupon rate for the new 10-year issue is set at 2.6 percent it will allow the 193rd JGB to be re-opened, traders said. "If the coupon rate is set at 2.6 percent, the new issue may eventually be merged with the 193rd 10-year JGB," a trader for a trust bank's securities unit said.
This may pave the way for the 193rd to become the new benchmark cash JGB, traders said.

Trade in the 190th JGB, which had been expected to take over the benchmark mantle from the 182nd JGB has been lacklustre and there is speculation that the 193rd may be better suited for that role, traders said.
